kind: primary philosophical paper; selected direct reading
title: Curie’s Truism
version: Philosophy of Science83(December2016),1014–1026; journal-layout author-hosted PDF.
locator: Selected §§1–2 and opening §3, journal pp1014–1018; rest not audited.
assumptions: Functional dependence and an explicit condition preserving the specified symmetries.
conclusion: Separates the elementary conditional symmetry lemma from the substantive task of instantiating it.
proof_status: Displayed lemma and selected surrounding argument read directly; no adoption of the entire causal-metaphysics thesis.
relevance: A direct prior formulation of the general inference used by Claude.
limits: Does not establish whether the sustaining-activity application has its own predecessor or settle temporal ontology.

kind: primary philosophical paper; selected direct reading
title: The simple failure of Curie’s Principle
version: Preprint dated6August2012,12pages. Later2013 journal article not collated.
locator: Selected §§1–2.3, preprint pp1–4, classical harmonic-oscillator counterexample.
assumptions: Standard classical state reversal T(q,p)=(q,−p); time-reversal-invariant oscillator dynamics.
conclusion: An initial T-fixed instantaneous state need not remain T-fixed at every later time.
proof_status: Classical example read directly and state-versus-history distinction independently checked; quantum and concluding sections not audited.
relevance: Prevents conflating instantaneous-state invariance during evolution with symmetry of a whole model and assigned window.
limits: Does not refute the whole-model equivariance lemma or settle the interpretive debate about time reversal.

kind: primary philosophical paper; selected direct reading
title: Which Curie’s Principle?
version: Author-hosted2016 preprint,14pages, not copyedited or formatted; version-of-record DOI10.1086/687933 not collated.
locator: Selected introduction and §4.2, preprint pp2,11–12; abstract also read.
assumptions: Their interpretation of intrinsic states and the transformations relevant to Curie’s principle.
conclusion: Distinguishes the original functional setting from the interstate formulation and contests standard time reversal as the relevant symmetry.
proof_status: Selected argument read directly as an author position; disagreement with Roberts not adjudicated globally.
relevance: Qualifies Claude’s identification of the lemma with a settled, uniformly interpreted physical principle.
limits: Not a blanket disproof of reasoning about explicitly defined reflections of whole histories; rest of paper not fully audited.

kind: primary philosophical paper; selected direct reading
title: Cosmology, Time’s Arrow, and That Old Double Standard
version: arXiv gr-qc/9310022v1,15October1993; later publication not collated.
assumptions: A symmetry-sensitive criticism of explanations of cosmological temporal asymmetry.
conclusion: Raises a double-standard objection to using direction-neutral reasoning to explain a temporal asymmetry.
proof_status: Selected framing read; cosmological derivations and later sections not audited.
relevance: Context for the diagnostic use distinguished from the elementary equivariance inference.
limits: Does not by the inspected passages supply a process-presence argument or verify novelty of its application.
